summary: This Old House demonstrates a complete under-sink reverse osmosis (RO) filtration installation. The video walks through what an RO system does (pre-filters, a central RO membrane cartridge, post-filter, and storage tank) and then shows a hands-on install: mounting cartridges inside a kitchen cabinet, reusing the existing faucet hole, routing tubing to barbed fittings, anchoring the assembly with a toggle-bolt base, tying the RO feed into the cold-water shut-off via a tee-style adapter (no soldering), tying the drain line into the sink drain with a provided adapter, connecting the storage tank, and finally powering up and testing the system. Along the way it highlights the filtration path (through pre-filter, membrane, post-filter, tank, and faucet), explains that only a limited amount of purified water is produced (drain waste ratio), and notes practical tradeoffs like the system supplying drinking water only. The transcript provides explicit step-by-step actions and tool usage (screwdriver, wrench, toggle bolt, barbed fittings) and the host emphasizes verification by tasting the output water.
